speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia. To understand the underlying cause, have you noticed any specific triggers, such as heat or infection, that worsen your symptoms? Additionally, do you experience weakness or difficulty speaking as well?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance and right-sided clumsiness suggest a focal neurological issue. Do you have any history of autoimmune conditions, like Sjögren's syndrome, or have you noticed any visual disturbances like blurry vision? Please also tell me if you experience any numbness, tingling, or pain in your limbs.

text: Since the initial inflammatory markers and imaging were normal, I need to clarify if your ataxia is truly static or if you experience relapses followed by periods of recovery, which is characteristic of Multiple Sclerosis. Have you noticed any episodes of optic neuritis, such as pain in one eye when moving it, or episodes of numbness that came and went?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Multiple sclerosis. The presence of Crohn's disease and the use of natalizumab, an immunomodulator often prescribed for both Crohn's and MS, alongside your history of gait ataxia, strongly support this diagnosis. Have you noticed any visual changes, such as blurred vision or color desaturation, since starting treatment?
